_readme: Hand-written arrival templates (PROTOTYPE_SCOPE: text is hand-written templates only). Placeholders in {braces}. Beat order: recognition, wrongness, personal echo, discovery (SYSTEMS §11). Selection rules: PROPOSED P0-13.

recognition.fountain.runs: You climb out of the machine in AD {year}. The Tiber smells the same. In the Subura, the district fountain you repaired still runs: the basin is worn smooth, and someone has cut two words into its rim: AQUA PURA.
recognition.fountain.dry: You climb out of the machine in AD {year}. The Tiber smells the same. You find the district fountain you repaired by the shape of the street, but the basin is cracked and dry, full of leaves.
recognition.workshop.working: You climb out of the machine in AD {year}. The Tiber smells the same. Near the Porta Trigemina you hear a single hammer: the smith's workshop you funded is still working, sooty and a little larger, with a boy asleep by the bellows.
recognition.workshop.street: You climb out of the machine in AD {year}. The Tiber smells the same. Near the Porta Trigemina you hear hammers: the smith's workshop you funded has become a whole street of forges, and over the oldest door hangs a painted sign with two fires.
recognition.workshop.gone: You climb out of the machine in AD {year}. The Tiber smells the same. Near the Porta Trigemina you find the smith's workshop you funded by its soot-black wall. It is a stable now.
recognition.neither: You climb out of the machine in AD {year}. The Tiber smells the same. You pass the corner where the smith worked and the fountain ran foul. Neither is there. You remember letting both chances pass.
recognition.unchosenFountain.fixed: Down the street, the fountain you didn't choose was repaired after all. Someone else did it.
recognition.unchosenFountain.foul: Down the street, the fountain you didn't choose was filled in long ago. An old woman calls the spot 'fever corner'.
recognition.unchosenWorkshop.later: The smith's forge, which you funded later, still smokes a few doors down.
recognition.unchosenWorkshop.gone: Of the smith you didn't choose, there is no trace.
recognition.unchosenFountain.laterRuns: Down the street, the fountain you repaired later still runs.
recognition.unchosenFountain.laterDry: Down the street, the fountain you repaired later has gone dry again; no one kept it up after you left.

wrongness.medicine.high: Something is wrong, and it takes you a moment to see it: children, everywhere. More than any Roman street you remember, and fewer small graves along the Via Appia.
wrongness.medicine.low: Something is wrong. Whole blocks of the Subura have fallen in, the streets are half-empty, and people cover their mouths when strangers pass.
wrongness.governance.high: Something is wrong. Magistrates post their rulings in the forum and people stop to read them. Nobody seems afraid of the soldiers.
wrongness.governance.low: Something is wrong. There are soldiers at every corner and they are not all the same army. People talk about emperors the way they talk about the weather.
wrongness.economy.high: Something is wrong. The cattle market has spilled over its walls; you hear six languages haggling over bales from half the world.
wrongness.economy.low: Something is wrong. The markets are thin, the stalls half empty, and bread costs a day's wage.
wrongness.asHistory: Something is wrong, and it takes you a while to name it: beyond the few things you recognize, this is Rome almost exactly as the history books describe AD {year}.

coin.sound: The denarius still rings true on the moneychangers' tables. Old men call it the one thing Rome never cheapened, and a few remember why: {coinHolder} would not let the mint cut the silver.
coin.debased: The coins are bronze washed thin with silver. The moneychangers weigh every one and trust none; the debasement you set in motion outran even Rome's own.
coin.historyDebased: The coins are lighter and paler than you remember, barely half silver now. Prices have climbed with every cut, and soldiers grumble that their pay buys less each year.
coin.historyMild: Coins pass a little lighter than you remember, a shade less silver in each, as Rome's mint has always done.

savings.carried: The {carried} aurei you carried are still in your purse, as good as the day you left.
savings.depositKept: At the banking house of Octavius a clerk finds your name in an old ledger. After some argument they honor it: {returned} aurei, with the interest of {years} years.
savings.depositLost: The banking house of Octavius is not what it was: {lostHow} Your deposit of {deposited} aurei is gone.
savings.hoardKept: You dig where you buried the jar. It is still there: {hoard} aurei, green with damp but gold underneath.
savings.hoardLost: Where you buried the jar there is a new wall and a bathhouse. Someone found your {hoard} aurei long before you came back.
savings.left: The {left} aurei you couldn't carry, and didn't hide or bank, are long gone.

personal.kept: In {keeper} you find a line carved over a door, in Demetria's Greek: 'For the one who stayed.' They don't know it means you.
personal.broken: In the oldest book of {keeper} there is a note in Demetria's hand: 'The foreigner promised to stay until the sickness passed. The sickness came in {outbreakYear}. The foreigner did not.'
personal.brokenNoKeeper: In a tomb inscription on the Via Latina you find Demetria's name, and a line she chose herself: 'I kept my promises.' You did not keep yours.
personal.refused: Demetria's letters survive in a library copy. One mentions you: 'The foreigner would not promise to stay. At least it was honest.'
personal.notOffered: You left before the first rumors came from the East. In the city's records, the pestilence of {outbreakYear} fills page after page: about {deaths} thousand dead in Rome. You aren't in any of them.
personal.notOfferedNoOutbreak: You left before the first rumors came from the East. You never learned whether Demetria would have asked you to stay.
personal.unanswered: Demetria's letters survive in a library copy. One mentions you: 'I asked the foreigner to stay until the sickness passed. I never had an answer.'
personal.neverAsked: Demetria's letters survive in a library copy. They name everyone who stayed to help the sick in {outbreakYear}. You are not among them; she never thought to ask you.
personal.office: In the hall of {officeHall} you find the roll of its officers. Between two names you don't know is a third, spelled wrong: yours, as {office}.
personal.founder: Over the door of {founded} someone has painted its beginning in red letters: 'Begun by a stranger from the East.'
personal.founderGone: Where {founded} stood there is a bathhouse now. The attendant has never heard of it.

discovery.circle.thriving: The Physicians' Circle of the Subura still meets by the fountain. They teach, argue about remedies, and keep a copy of your charter under glass. Its head is {leader}.
discovery.circle.drifted: The circle you backed with Demetria is now {pathName}. {pathDescription} Its head, {leader}, speaks of the founders as a legend.
discovery.circle.dissolved: The Physicians' Circle is gone. One inscription remains, built into the wall of a newer house.
discovery.circle.rogue: The circle you backed is now {pathName}. {pathDescription} They know who you are, and they do not want you back.
discovery.faction.thriving: The Caecilian faction still sits together in the Curia, still arguing for honest courts. Its leader is {leader}.
discovery.faction.drifted: The senate faction you backed with Varro is now {pathName}. {pathDescription}
discovery.faction.captured: The senate faction you backed with Varro is now {pathName}. {pathDescription} Its head is {leader}.
discovery.faction.dissolved: Of the Caecilian faction nothing remains but a family tomb.
discovery.faction.rogue: The senate faction you backed is now {pathName}. {pathDescription} They know who you are, and they do not want you back.
discovery.none: You ask at the guild halls and the Curia whether anyone remembers you. No one does: you never held enough of anything in Rome to leave your mark on it.
discovery.circle.corrupted: The Physicians' Circle still has a door and a name, but it licenses whoever pays. Its head, {leader}, answers to other people now.
discovery.faction.corrupted: The Caecilian faction still votes as a bloc, but its votes are for sale. Its head is {leader}.
discovery.corruption.minor: Its accounts show a gap from the years after you left: some of the gold you left was quietly skimmed (minor corruption).
discovery.corruption.major: Its records tell of a great embezzlement a generation after you left: half the treasury vanished and the payments you arranged stopped (major corruption).
discovery.corruption.total: Everyone knows the story: within a generation of your leaving, its whole treasury was stolen, and those who took it took the institution too (total corruption).
discovery.guild.thriving: The Merchants' Guild of Ostia still meets at the harbor, still arguing for open markets and honest coin. Its head is {leader}.
discovery.guild.drifted: The guild you backed at Ostia is now {pathName}. {pathDescription} Its head is {leader}.
discovery.guild.captured: The guild you backed at Ostia is now {pathName}. {pathDescription} Its head is {leader}.
discovery.guild.dissolved: Of the Merchants' Guild of Ostia nothing remains but a name carved on a warehouse lintel.
discovery.guild.rogue: The guild you backed is now {pathName}. {pathDescription} They know who you are, and they do not want you back.
discovery.guild.corrupted: The Merchants' Guild still has its hall at Ostia, but its treasury was emptied long ago and its seats are for sale. Its head is {leader}.
discovery.generic.thriving: {name}, which {how}, is still there and still itself. Its head is {leader}.
discovery.generic.drifted: {name}, which {how}, is now {pathName}. {pathDescription} Its head is {leader}.
discovery.generic.captured: {name}, which {how}, is now {pathName}. {pathDescription} Its head is {leader}.
discovery.generic.corrupted: {name}, which {how}, still has its name and its door, but its treasury was emptied long ago and its seats are for sale. Its head is {leader}.
discovery.generic.dissolved: Of {name}, which {how}, nothing remains but a name no one recognizes.
discovery.generic.rogue: {name}, which {how}, is now {pathName}. {pathDescription} They know who you are, and they do not want you back.
discovery.office: You served it as {office}; your name is still on the roll.
discovery.orders.strong.held: They still read your parting words aloud at {short}'s meetings, and {camp} still lead it.
discovery.orders.strong.lost: Your parting words were copied out and honored for a generation; then {camp} lost anyway.
discovery.orders.some.held: Some remember what you asked of {short} before you left; {camp} lead it, as you wanted.
discovery.orders.some.lost: Some remember what you asked of {short} before you left. It didn't hold: {camp} are not the ones in charge.
discovery.orders.weak.held: No one at {short} remembers the foreigner's advice, but {camp} lead it all the same.
discovery.orders.weak.lost: No one at {short} remembers the foreigner's advice; {camp} lost the argument long ago.

walk.intro: You can walk around Rome: visit market, changers, forges, curia or subura (no Attention).
walk.market.start: You follow the noise downhill to a cattle market by the river: the Forum Boarium, if you remember your Latin inscriptions. Nobody here has ever seen a zipper, and several people stare. You work out prices by watching: a modius of wheat, about a bucket's worth, costs {wheat} denarii, and the man hauling sacks earns {wage} a day, about {kg} kg of wheat. You have no denarii. You have gold.
walk.market.high: The Forum Boarium has spilled past its old walls; stalls sell cloth, glass and spice from half the world.
walk.market.asHistory: The Forum Boarium is busy and loud, much as you left it.
walk.market.low: The Forum Boarium is half empty; many stalls are shuttered, and the cattle pens stand open.
walk.market.prices: A modius of wheat costs about {wheat} denarii (it was {wheatThen} when you left); a laborer earns about {wage} a day, enough for about {kg} kg of wheat (then {kgThen} kg).
walk.changers: At the money changers' tables an aureus fetches {aureus} denarii{aureusThen}. They reckon the denarius {silver}% silver{silverThen}. {trust}
walk.changers.trust.good: They take it without a second look.
walk.changers.trust.fair: They bite the coins and grumble, but take them.
walk.changers.trust.poor: They weigh every coin twice and trust nothing but gold.
walk.forges.start: Down by the Porta Trigemina a smith is swearing at a cracked bellows: one forge, one apprentice, too much work. He looks at your strange boots, then at your purse, and says he could use a partner. Out at Ostia, people say, the Merchants' Guild runs the harbor under a man called Publius Aelius Sabinus.
walk.forges.workshop.high: By the Porta Trigemina the smith's workshop you funded has become a whole street of forges.
walk.forges.workshop.asHistory: By the Porta Trigemina the smith's workshop you funded is still working, a little larger than you left it.
walk.forges.apprentices: The masters here learned from men who learned from your apprentices. They still work the way you showed the first of them, and swear it's the only way.
walk.forges.workshop.low: By the Porta Trigemina the smith's workshop you funded has shrunk to a single cold forge.
walk.forges.noWorkshop: By the Porta Trigemina the smiths work as they always have.
walk.forges.inUse: You see your ideas in use: {inventions}.
walk.curia.start: You find the Senate house by following the togas. Inside, two factions, the Caecilians and the Junians, trade speeches while the emperor's officials watch. So it is AD 155: Antoninus Pius is old, the empire is at peace, and in ten years a pestilence will come back from the East with the legions. Only you know that.
walk.curia.high: The Curia is orderly; petitions are heard in turn, and the magistrates' notices are posted and kept.
walk.curia.asHistory: The Curia is as it ever was: factions, favors, and petitions that wait.
walk.curia.low: The Curia is half deserted; the magistrates' notices are torn down, and men settle disputes with their fists.
walk.curia.policy: The line you left is still spoken of: {policy}.
walk.subura.start: You came down in the Subura: crowded, loud and poor, one corner of a city of about {population} people. The district fountain runs brown, and a mother pulls her child away from it. Somewhere behind you, in the rubble of a storeroom, is everything you have left of your own century.
walk.subura.high: The Subura is still crowded, but cleaner than you remember; fewer children look sick.
walk.subura.asHistory: The Subura is crowded and poor, much as you left it.
walk.subura.low: The Subura is dirtier than you left it; fevers come every summer.
walk.subura.fountain.dry: The district fountain is dry and cracked.
walk.subura.fountain.foul: The district fountain still runs brown.
walk.subura.population: About {population} people live in the city (about {populationThen} when you left).
walk.use.triphammer: a water-driven hammer pounds beside the river
walk.use.lathe: treadle lathes turn axles and spindles
walk.use.bellows: water wheels work the forge bellows
walk.use.furnace: molten iron is poured into sand moulds
walk.use.bookkeeping: merchants keep their books in double entry
walk.use.bills: traders settle debts with written bills
walk.use.audit: the city's accounts are read aloud each year
walk.use.soap: healers wash with soap and boil their linen
walk.use.spirits: surgeons clean wounds with distilled wine
walk.use.ward: a fever ward keeps its sick apart and writes down every case
walk.changers.bills: Traders pass written bills across the tables as readily as coin.
walk.intro.start: Your ears still ring from the crash. Before anything else you could walk and get your bearings: visit market, changers, forges, curia or subura (no Attention).
walk.changers.start: At a table a man weighs coins on a little balance and bites them. You show him an aureus from your purse, and his eyebrows go up: {aureus} denarii, he says, the official rate, less his cut. The silver coins in his tray are about {silver}% silver, and he takes them without a second look. You're going to be doing this a lot.
walk.forges.start.partner: Down by the Porta Trigemina the smith you've just paid is clearing space for a second forge, still swearing at his cracked bellows. He calls you 'partner' as if testing the word. Out at Ostia, people say, the Merchants' Guild runs the harbor under a man called Publius Aelius Sabinus.

recognition2.fountain.runs: You climb out again in AD {year}, {gap} years after your last visit and a minute after it for you. The fountain in the Subura still runs. Its basin has been replaced; the new one has a lion's-head spout, and the children still fight over it.
recognition2.fountain.dry: You climb out again in AD {year}, {gap} years after your last visit. The fountain in the Subura is dry; a cobbler has built his stall against the basin and keeps his lasts in it.
recognition2.workshop.working: You climb out again in AD {year}, {gap} years after your last visit. The forge by the Porta Trigemina still smokes; the family who run it now have never heard of a partner who drew machines on wax.
recognition2.workshop.street: You climb out again in AD {year}, {gap} years after your last visit. The street of forges near the Porta Trigemina has spread down to the river. No one there remembers the first smith, but they still turn axles the way he did.
recognition2.workshop.gone: You climb out again in AD {year}, {gap} years after your last visit. Near the Porta Trigemina the old forge has fallen in; weeds grow through the hearth where your smith worked.
recognition2.neither: You climb out again in AD {year}, {gap} years after your last visit. The corner where the smith worked and the fountain ran foul is a tavern now. It has no idea it could have been anything else.
recognition2.unchosenFountain.fixed: The fountain down the street still runs; the plaque on it names a magistrate you never met.
recognition2.unchosenFountain.foul: 'Fever corner' is still what they call the spot where the fountain was.
recognition2.unchosenWorkshop.later: The forge you funded later has a grandson's name over its door now.
recognition2.unchosenWorkshop.gone: Of the smith there is still no trace.
recognition2.unchosenFountain.laterRuns: The fountain you repaired late still runs, patched with newer stone.
recognition2.unchosenFountain.laterDry: The fountain you repaired late is dry again.

personal2.kept: The house with 'For the one who stayed' over its door has been rebuilt and the line is gone. But the street association still holds a supper each autumn it calls the stayer's supper, and no one can tell you why.
personal2.broken: Demetria's note about the foreigner who didn't stay has become a saying in {keeper}: 'to promise like the foreigner'. It means to mean well and leave.
personal2.brokenNoKeeper: Demetria's tomb on the Via Latina has lost its inscription to the weather. You are the only one left who knows what it said.
personal2.refused: Demetria's letters are still copied in the libraries. Scholars argue about the foreigner who wouldn't promise to stay; most think she made you up.
personal2.notOffered: The pestilence of {outbreakYear} is an old story now, told to frighten children. Your name was never part of it.
personal2.notOfferedNoOutbreak: No one remembers the Greek physician of the Subura. You never met her; you left too soon.
personal2.unanswered: A scholar has found Demetria's letter about the foreigner who never answered her. He thinks it's a riddle. It isn't.
personal2.neverAsked: Demetria's list of those who stayed in {outbreakYear} is carved on a wall now, in a portico by the Tiber. You read it twice. You are not on it.
personal2.office: Your name is still on the roll of {officeHall}'s officers, worn almost smooth where people touch it for luck.
personal2.founder: {Founded} keeps the day of its beginning as a feast. They pour a cup for the stranger who began it, and leave it full.
personal2.founderGone: No one you ask has heard of {founded}.

wrongness2.medicine.high: The streets are louder than you left them: children again, everywhere, and old people too, more of them than any Roman street should hold.
wrongness2.medicine.low: The city is thinner than you left it. Doors are chalked with the marks of sickness, and the burial clubs have queues.
wrongness2.governance.high: The Forum is still orderly. Rulings are posted and read, and when soldiers pass, people step aside without hurrying.
wrongness2.governance.low: The Forum has changed hands again; you can tell from the fresh names chiselled over old ones. The soldiers at the corners wear three different badges.
wrongness2.economy.high: The markets have grown past anything you left: new warehouses along the river, and moneychangers who quote rates for cities you've never heard of.
wrongness2.economy.low: The markets have shrunk since you left. Half the stalls are shuttered, and the rest trade in kind as often as for money.
wrongness2.asHistory: You look for what has changed since your last visit and find almost nothing you didn't expect: Rome in AD {year} is the Rome of the history books.

coin2.sound: The denarius still rings true. It's become a point of pride: shopkeepers bite coins in front of foreigners to show there's nothing to hide.
coin2.debased: The coins are worse than when you last came: bronze with a wash of silver that rubs off in your purse.
coin2.historyDebased: The coins are worse again: grey, light, barely silver at all. Prices are quoted in bundles of coins now, not single ones.
coin2.historyMild: The coins are a shade lighter again, as Rome's mint has always done.
